subject: Different linetype for different geoms in legend

messages.author: a3266bb8f38fd78e
messages.subject: Different linetype for different geoms in legend
parts:
Hi there !

I recently discouvered ggplot and I like how the plots look, so now I
want to change older plots to ggplot, but I have some difficulties
doing that.

So I would like that for the three items in the legend, the same
symbols appear as were used for plotting them.

Here is the code:
x <-
c(1.9999999,1.9999998,1.9999997,1.9999996,14.0000001,14.0000002,14.0000003,14.0000004)
y <- c(567.385, 569.415, 560.280, 570.430, 501.410, 499.380, 503.440,
504.455)
xrange <- range(c(1,14))
yrange <- range(c(y,470))

legend<-as.factor(c("measurements","regression line","value"))

dat <- data.frame( x , y)

p <- ggplot(dat ,aes(x,y,linetype=lty,shape=shapes)) + xlab("Column")+
ylab("Size")
p <- p + ylim(yrange) +
geom_point(aes(colour=legend[1],shape=20,linetype=0))
p <- p +
stat_smooth(method=lm,aes(colour=legend[2],shape=1,linetype=1))
p <- p +
geom_abline(intercept=480,slope=0,aes(colour=legend[3],shape=1,linetype=2))
p <- p +
opts(legend.position=c(0.75,0.92),legend.background=theme_blank())
p <- p + scale_colour_manual("",c(2,3,4))

I tried various approaches, but so far nothing worked.

Thanks,
Simon

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Different linetype for different geoms in legend
parts:
Here's a more minimal example:

dat <- structure(list(x = c(1.9999999, 1.9999998, 1.9999997, 1.9999996,
14.0000001, 14.0000002, 14.0000003, 14.0000004), y = c(567.385,
569.415, 560.28, 570.43, 501.41, 499.38, 503.44, 504.455)), .Names = c("x",
"y"), row.names = c(NA, -8L), class = "data.frame")

ggplot(dat, aes(x,y)) +
geom_point(aes(colour = "measurement")) +
stat_smooth(aes(colour = "smooth"), method = lm) +
geom_hline(aes(colour = "mean", yintercept=480))

And I think the problem is that you only want (e.g.) points in the
legend for measurement.

This is bug http://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/#issue/5, and it's
a tricky one.

Hadley

Thanks for your quick answer !
As long as the bug isn't fixed, I think I can live with the present
state :)

I think that it's not like you intended ggplot to be, but maybe you
could add a function like legend_manual() which works like the
standard legend() and lets you specifiy everything.

Simon
